title: A red smoke tier is not yet evidence, because the tier inherits the create race
foundBy: session agent, after chasing a smoke failure to host timing rather than to the change under test
details:
`make ci` fails intermittently for reasons unrelated to the change being tested. Its smoke tier boots real machines, so it inherits the race recorded in SAC-007.

The tier is the last gate `make ci` runs. A red result therefore arrives after every cheap check has passed, and the natural reading is that the change broke something. It usually has not.

Reproducing the failure is the trap. The race is decided by how fast a guest boots, which depends on host load and on the storage the working tree sits on. Comparing two commits across that difference measures the storage rather than the commits.

These numbers come from diagnosing SAC-007. Four of six runs on an ext4 tree failed at least one scenario. Three consecutive runs on a tmpfs tree failed none, and a later run on a second tmpfs tree failed two. Storage therefore shifts the odds without deciding the outcome, which is what makes a two-commit comparison so easy to misread.

Fixing SAC-007 removes most of this. What remains is worth a sentence in CONTRIBUTING. A red smoke tier is first a reason to run the tier again on the same tree. Suspecting the diff comes after that.
